items.title: Akiyoshi Toshiko — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Miles‟ group was Paul Chambers and Red Garland, uh, Philly Joe [Jones]

ctx.x: What did you think of Richie‟s playing? Did you hear him much?

Yeah, he played … you know, played well, just like everybody else. Actually, I liked, I liked … the first time when I was here, Miles‟ group was Paul Chambers and Red Garland, uh, Philly Joe [Jones]. That was something. I really thought it was … that was like a modern, what do you call, Basie‟s famous, you know, rhythm section, except no guitar player. But uh, it was really fantastic.
Was Coltrane in the group, too?

items.title: Toshiko Akiyoshi interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 17, 1999
items.q: Even for example the greatest classic Miles Davis Quintet, like Red Garland, Philly Jo, Coltrane, Paul Chambers.

ctx.x: No. Actually I never thought about it until Duke Ellington died. Before that, you know it was just a Japanese traditional concept, or being Japanese playing jazz was some sort of a handicap. When I was growing up in Japan as a player, they always said that Filipino people have better feeling than Japanese, and indeed the Filipino players played better than us, and it’s simply because they have a longer history. They weren’t under — they were colonized by America so they are more exposed for jazz, much longer than…
